Limits and what is not possible yet

This page lists every fixed limit on a VMnodes app, and everything a builder cannot do on their own today, with what to do instead. Read it before you promise a customer a feature, and when something you expected is missing.

Where a row says "your VMnodes contact", that person at VMnodes can do it for you; the portal and the app cannot.

Limit or not possible yetTodayWhat to do instead
Creating an orgNeeds an invite code.Ask your VMnodes contact for an invite code.
Inviting a second personNo portal screen. The person must already be a member of the org.Ask your VMnodes contact to invite them.
Creating a groupThe portal can attach an existing group to an app, not create one.Ask your VMnodes contact to create the group, then attach it on the People tab.
API tokensBuilders cannot create them.Ask your VMnodes contact. An app that shares data gets its own token automatically; see Publish and query API.
Secrets and environment variables you choosevmnodes.json has no key for them, and the portal has no screen.Keep configuration in the app, or in its database. The platform's own variables are on Environment variables.
Reading another app's shared dataNeeds a grant made by your VMnodes contact, and a token.Ask your VMnodes contact for access to the entity by name. A portal app that publishes nothing has no token.
Mail, AI, directory and Xero connectionsNot available to a portal app.Ask your VMnodes contact. The manifest path can ask for some of them.
The manifest pathYour VMnodes contact signs, submits and approves.Give them the manifest and the image.
A public app, one anyone can openNot available. Everyone who opens an app must be a member of the org with access.Give each person access on the People tab.
Stopping and starting an appNo portal button.Ask your VMnodes contact.
Disconnecting GitHubNo screen. An org connects one GitHub account.Ask your VMnodes contact.
Python or another language without a DockerfileDepends on how the platform is set up.Commit a Dockerfile; see Build, run and security checks.
Scan settingWhether critical findings block a deploy is set by VMnodes.Fix critical findings either way; see Security scan.
Repository layoutThe app is at the repository root; no subdirectories or monorepos.Move the app to the root of its own repository.
Branch and repository on updateUpdate to latest commit uses the latest commit of the default branch of the repository the app was launched from. It cannot be changed.Merge into the default branch, then update.
Updates at onceOne per app at a time.Wait for the running one to finish.
Who sees what in the portalA member who is not an administrator sees the Overview tab only.Ask an administrator to do what needs the other tabs.
Port3000, fixed, and the app must listen on all addresses.Listen on 3000.
Memory and CPUFixed: 2048 MiB maximum memory, a CPU share of 512.Keep the app within them.
Data kept in the containerCleared on every update.Set "database": true and keep data there. See Environment variables.
LogsThe Console shows the last 50 lines; the files rotate at 10 MB, three kept.Log what you need to find a fault, and keep it short.
vmnodes.json size64 KiB.Keep roles short.
App name3 to 30 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not reserved. See Build, run and security checks.Pick another name.
Role nameOne or two segments joined by a dot, each 2 to 31 characters.See vmnodes.json reference.
A role added by an updateNobody holds it until an administrator gives it.Give it on the People tab with Change roles.
Records per publish call1000.Send in batches. In snapshot mode a batch that is only part of the list marks the rest as deleted, so use upsert for batches.
Publish and query requests300 requests a minute, and 1 MiB per request.Batch and cache.
Query rows50 by default, at most 200 per query. Grouped results are cut at 200 groups. The in filter takes 1 to 100 values.Filter and aggregate.
Launch scan wait10 minutes. Boot window for the first health check: 60 seconds.Make the app answer /health quickly.
